title: A managed organization is updated without a person in the loop
description:
**Phase 4 of 5.**

- **Blocked by:** the release record story and the ordering story
- **Runs in parallel with:** the notification story
- **Unblocks:** nothing

---
What the $20 buys, delivered. Chatticus assumes the cross-account role and applies the release to the customer deployment. No ticket, no session, no email asking them to schedule something.

Two constraints that are the whole story:

**It does not interrupt work in flight.** An update that kills a running turn is an outage the customer did not schedule and cannot explain to whoever was waiting on it.

**It rolls back.** A rapidly-evolving beta applying automatic updates to production deployments in accounts Anthus does not own needs a rollback path before it needs a faster rollout. The failure to design against is a release breaking a customer organization while everyone at Anthus is asleep.

**Done when:** the scenarios exist and fail for the right reason.

comments.author: unknown
comments.text:
Feature: Managed updates

  Scenario: A managed organization receives a release automatically
    Given a managed organization behind the current release
    And that release is running at Anthus
    When the rollout reaches that organization
    Then its deployment is updated
    And it records the new release

  Scenario: An update waits for work in flight to finish
    Given a managed organization with a turn in progress
    When the rollout reaches that organization
    Then the turn completes
    And the update is applied afterwards

  Scenario: A failed update rolls back
    Given a managed organization being updated
    When the update fails
    Then the deployment is returned to its previous release
    And an operator is alerted
